summary: Specifies an option for the IP header that lets a datagram collect timestamps as it travels, so you can see when it passed through each point. It is a measurement aid for the Internet Protocol.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 781 defines an IP header option for recording timestamps as a packet travels through a catenet. A destination can inspect the recorded times, provided the participating clocks are synchronized.

subtitle: An IP option that records timestamps as a packet passes through gateways.

tldr.problem: Measuring delays across interconnected packet networks requires timestamp information from devices along the packet's path.
tldr.mechanism: The IP timestamp option provides space for timestamps and optional Internet IDs, with fields for offset, overflow, and mode flags.
tldr.outcome: The memo specifies the option format and notes that one-way delay measurement depends on synchronized device clocks.

today: RFC 781 specifies a timestamp option for the Internet Protocol. Its stated purpose is measuring catenet delay, with synchronized clocks assumed.

sections.title: Measuring Delay Across Networks
sections.content:
Packet-switched networks store and forward packets, so their delays vary. The memo says measuring those delays across gateways and member networks is important for catenet investigations.

It proposes timestamping packet headers for both user traffic and test packets. Measuring one-way delay requires synchronized clocks in the gateways and hosts involved.
sections.plainLanguage: A packet's travel time can vary across interconnected networks. Recording times at gateways can help measure that delay, but the clocks must be synchronized.

sections.title: Timestamp Option Fields
sections.content:
The option uses type 68 decimal and has a maximum length of 40 octets. Its control fields include an offset to the next timestamp space, an overflow count for IP modules unable to add a timestamp, and flags selecting timestamp-only, ID-plus-timestamp, or pre-specified-ID operation.

Each timestamp is a right-justified 32-bit value in milliseconds modulo 24 hours from midnight UT. The option is not copied during fragmentation and is carried in the first fragment.
sections.plainLanguage: The option records times and can also record or check the Internet ID of the device adding each time. Its fields show where the next timestamp goes and whether devices ran out of space.

sections.title: Timestamping and Available Space
sections.content:
In timestamp-only mode, an IP module records a timestamp. In the mode that includes Internet IDs, each timestamp is preceded by the registering entity's ID. In the prespecified-ID mode, a module records its timestamp only when the next ID matches its own.

When there is no more header space for timestamps, the offset indicates that condition and the overflow field counts modules that cannot register.
sections.plainLanguage: Depending on the flag, a device can add only its time, add its ID and time, or add time only when its ID is expected. The option also records when space runs out.
